title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1973-11-30

ai_review.summary: Audience‑recorded show with rough sound but stellar performances – Morning Dew opener, Black Throated Wind and an epic Eyes of the World.
ai_review.review: The concert is praised for its high‑energy first set opener (a soaring Morning Dew) and a second half packed with memorable jams, especially a near‑legendary Eyes of the World that builds into a Dark Star/Slipknot stretch.  The audience recording is described as hissy, harsh and at times bass‑poor, yet listeners consider it worth hearing for the musical moments.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews consistently highlight an excellent performance (many 4–5 ★) while noting only moderate‑to‑poor recording quality; the weighted average yields a solid four‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy, harsh and crowd‑heavy sound; described as 'tin cans on a string', bass‑light, occasional drop‑outs (e.g., Sugar Magnolia) and uneven clarity in parts of the set.

poor_songs: Sugar Magnolia (cut out before Sunshine Daydream)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set launches with a long, powerful Morning Dew and moves through upbeat rockers; the second set mirrors that energy with Bertha into Promised Land, then shifts into extended jams culminating in an outstanding Eyes of the World/Dark Star sequence.
